chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit, from Amr ibn Jumay' — he raised it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him):

He was asked about dueling (al-mubarazah) between the two lines of troops without the Imam's permission. He said: 'There is no harm in it, but that is not sought/undertaken except with the permission of the Imam.'

key_terms.الْمُبَارَزَة: Dueling or individual combat between champions of two armies

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on individual dueling (mubarazah) in Islamic battles?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *al-mubarazah* (champion combat), distinguishing between the permissibility of the act itself and the necessity of the Imam's specific authorization for its deployment. In Shia scholarly tradition, this highlights the Imam's central role in military strategy, ensuring that such high-stakes engagements serve the broader tactical objectives of the community rather than individual glory.
